target: fatal accidents involving Boeing commercial jets

records.source_publisher: National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), United States
records.decision_reason: As ICAO Annex 13 accredited representative for the State of Design and Manufacture, NTSB records the Pegasus PC2193 Boeing 737-800 runway-excursion accident and three passenger fatalities, and states that the Turkish investigation was completed.

reconciliation_evidence.observation: IATA independently lists Pegasus B737-800 on 5 February 2020 as a jet hull-loss runway-excursion accident with three onboard fatalities.

records.operation_type: commercial passenger repatriation flight under Vande Bharat Mission
records.decision_reason: India AAIB identifies the Air India Express B737-800 VT-AXH occurrence at Kozhikode as a landing runway-excursion accident and records 21 fatalities.

reconciliation_evidence.record: IATA Safety Report 2020 / Air India Express B737-800
reconciliation_evidence.observation: IATA independently lists the 7 August 2020 Air India Express B737-800 VT-AXH passenger jet as a hull-loss runway-excursion accident; its 2020 report records two fatal runway excursions totaling 24 fatalities, consistent with this event and PC2193.

records.location: near Tehran Imam Khomeini International Airport, Iran
records.accident_class: target-taxonomy unresolved: Annex 13 accident / unlawful-security act in IATA statistics
records.source_publisher: Aircraft Accident Investigation Board of the Islamic Republic of Iran; copy hosted by ICAO
records.decision_reason: The Annex 13 final report describes the Boeing 737-800 commercial-flight occurrence as an accident caused by interference of military activity with civil aviation operations, while IATA explicitly excludes PS752 from accident statistics as an unlawful act. The frozen BSFM target wording does not explicitly resolve this security/unlawful-act boundary, so no favorable retrospective inclusion or exclusion is allowed.

reconciliation_evidence.observation: IATA identifies the PS752 shoot-down and explicitly states that it is considered an unlawful act and therefore belongs to aviation-security statistics rather than the report's accident statistics.

records.location: Kepulauan Seribu area, DKI Jakarta, Indonesia
records.source_publisher: Komite Nasional Keselamatan Transportasi (KNKT), Republic of Indonesia
records.decision_reason: KNKT identifies the occurrence as the accident of Sriwijaya Air SJY182, Boeing 737-500 PK-CLC, on a scheduled passenger flight. Independent IATA accident data records 62 onboard fatalities.

reconciliation_evidence.record: Accidents Update: as of 30 June 2021 / Sriwijaya Air
reconciliation_evidence.observation: IATA independently lists the 9 January 2021 Sriwijaya Air B737-500 as a jet hull-loss accident with 62 onboard fatalities and loss-of-control-in-flight category.

records.location: near Molang Village, Teng County, Wuzhou, Guangxi, China
records.decision_reason: The competent state aviation authority identifies the occurrence as the MU5735 aviation accident, a Boeing 737-800 scheduled passenger flight, and records that all 123 passengers and nine crew members died.

reconciliation_evidence.record: Accident Report Update 2022 Mid-Year / 2022-03-21 China Eastern Airlines
reconciliation_evidence.observation: IATA independently lists the 21 March 2022 China Eastern Airlines B737-800 as a jet hull-loss accident with 132 onboard fatalities.

records.location: south of Myanmar; diverted to Bangkok, Thailand
records.source_publisher: Singapore Ministry of Transport / Transport Safety Investigation Bureau
records.decision_reason: Official TSIB interim statement identifies a scheduled Singapore Airlines Boeing B777 flight, classed by TSIB as an accident, with one passenger death.

reconciliation_evidence.record: 2024 Statistical Summary / 2024 Airplane Accidents / Singapore Airlines 777-300ER
reconciliation_evidence.observation: Worldwide commercial-jet event table independently lists the 21 May 2024 Singapore Airlines 777-300ER scheduled-passenger accident with one onboard fatality.

records.source_publisher: Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Lithuania, Transport Accident and Incident Investigation Division
records.decision_reason: Official Lithuanian investigation update identifies the Swiftair Boeing 737-476/737-400SF accident and states that the aircraft pilot died; the investigated flight was a commercial cargo operation.

reconciliation_evidence.observation: Worldwide commercial-jet event table independently lists the 25 November 2024 Swiftair 737-400 charter-cargo accident at Vilnius with one onboard fatality.

records.source_publisher: Republic of Korea Aviation and Railway Accident Investigation Board (ARAIB)
records.decision_reason: The competent Korean investigation authority identifies the 29 December 2024 Jeju Air HL8088 accident at Muan as a B737-800 occurrence; its preliminary report records 179 fatalities and two serious injuries.

reconciliation_evidence.record: 2024 Statistical Summary / 2024 Airplane Accidents / Jeju Air 737-800
reconciliation_evidence.observation: Worldwide commercial-jet event table independently lists the 29 December 2024 Jeju Air 737-800 scheduled-passenger accident at Muan with 179 onboard fatalities.

reconciliation_evidence.publisher: Bureau d'Enquêtes et d'Analyses pour la sécurité de l'aviation civile (BEA)
reconciliation_evidence.observation: BEA identifies South Korea ARAIB as responsible entity and records Boeing 737, HL8088, commercial passenger operation and 179 deaths.
